title: Run a dead-weight gauge test: load, float and spin the weights, then trim the gauge
instruction: Load both weights onto the piston, pump until the orange flag is in the green band, spin the weights, turn the blue knob while they spin until the gauge needle is on the red mark, and move both hands away.
context: Instrument technicians check pressure gauges against a dead-weight tester: weights on a piston set a known pressure, the operator pumps until the piston floats, and spins the weights so piston friction doesn't falsify the reading before comparing the gauge.
setup: A calibration bench on the table, positions in cm from the arm bases' midpoint in x and the table's centre line in y, +y toward the left arm. A dead-weight tester's steel column 3.2 cm square at (30, -10) carries a platen 4.4 cm square, its top 2.5 cm above the table, with a steel stem 1.6 cm square and 5.65 cm tall above it, topped by a purple spin cross of two bars 6.6 x 1.6 x 1 cm. Piston and spin assembly 250 g. Two brass slotted weights, each 7 cm across, 1.6 cm thick, 324 g, with a 3 cm wide slot from 1.5 cm behind the centre out to the edge, lie slot toward +x across pairs of steel rails 5 x 1 x 3 cm tall with centres 4 cm apart, at (20, -20) and (20, -30). The pump lever, steel with a red pad 5.6 cm square, pivots at (15, 25) 4.5 cm above the table, is 18.5 cm long along +x, sprung up to 18 degrees above level and goes down to 4 degrees below. The test gauge lies face up at (43, 10), a white dial 11 cm across with a black needle and a red mark toward +x. Its trim knob at (33, 10) has a blue wing 5.2 x 1.6 x 2 cm, top 7.8 cm above the table, and turns 110 degrees either way. Beyond the column a white plate at y = -10 carries a green band and an orange flag 4 x 1.2 cm that travels from x = 38.5 cm, 2 cm per cm of piston rise. Simulated hydraulics: a full stroke raises the oil level 1 cm, and the oil acts as a 420 N/m spring under the real load, so with both weights the piston stays on its stop for two strokes and floats about 2.75 cm up after five. The needle moves 16.7 degrees per N carried and 0.6 degrees per knob degree; with the full load floating and freed it starts 40 degrees short of the mark, and piston motion without spin adds or subtracts 25 degrees until spun. The screenshot shows the start.
scoring: Read at the end of the run; no early end. A hand is a gripper's fingertip midpoint, and a weight counts as let go with both hands 6 cm or more from its box in its own frame. 0 for good if the piston rises 5 cm or a weight falls off the table. Otherwise 0.15 for each weight let go with the stem in its slot, flat within 5 degrees, resting within 4 mm of the platen or of the other weight; the weights are interchangeable. 0.3 with both on. 0.5 with the piston also 2.1 to 3.7 cm up (flag in the green band). 0.75 with the weights also spun since the piston last moved: both weights and the cross at 2 rad/s or more, both on the stem and the piston floating 5 mm or more up; moving the piston 1.5 mm unspun undoes it. 0.9 with the needle also within 5 degrees of the red mark and the knob last moved (by 2 degrees or more) while they spun at that rate. 1.0 with the lever also within 3 degrees of its top, both hands 8 cm or more from the knob and the lever's pad, and piston, lever, knob and weights at rest for the last 1 s (under 1 cm/s up or down, 5 degrees/s for lever and knob, 0.5 rad/s tilting; the spin itself may continue).
reset_notes: Put the weights back on their rails, release the oil so the piston is on its stop, and turn the knob back to its start. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation. Oil compliance is a soft spring: the weights' real mass sinks the piston; strokes raise the target. No release valve. Spin is real: a hand strikes the cross, friction carries the weights, decay 20 s. Piston friction is coded: a needle error of 25 degrees, far larger than life, set by unspun motion and cleared by real spin. Needle and flag are read-outs without colliders.
